intro: Elaiussa Sebaste, an ancient city in Mersin province, spans the 2nd century BC to the 7th century AD. Picture a Roman island city on the Mersin coast, with its theatre and its cisterns.
history: The city was founded as a trading colony in the 2nd century BC and grew with the support of the Cappadocian king Archelaus. Linked to the land by an isthmus, and graced with its theatre, agora and churches, it became one of Cilicia's important ports.
structure-3: You are now at the cisterns: underground reservoirs that stored rain and spring water. Think of the care it took to keep a whole city supplied.
structure-5: Now you stand before the Monumental Tomb, erected for an important person or dynasty. Pause for a moment: someone wished to be remembered here.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Theatre and the Agora, and save a moment for the Church.
facts: Did you know? The city's name means 'olive city', and the island's olive trees still bear fruit today. The city began on an islet; when the channel silted up, the island joined the shore and the city spread onto it. King Archelaus of Cappadocia made it his second capital and renamed it Sebaste in honour of Augustus. Today theatre, baths and basilica line up along the shore, with the modern road running straight through them.
outro: This brings our tour of Elaiussa Sebaste to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Enjoy your visit.
